title: Kaboom Crew ragdoll foundation — template + bootstrap registration
notes: First slice of GDP-2026-05-24-002 (Kaboom Crew migration to the engine ragdoll module). This sprint lands the foundation only: enables physics in the project, ships the kaboom-bomber template, registers it at bootstrap. The actual DEATH PATH migration (replacing S105 spring math with a RagdollSpawnRequest on alive=false flip) ships in S130 — a separate sprint so we can validate the foundation is clean first.

Risk profile: enabling physics adds Rapier WASM to the kaboom-crew bundle + runs the physics-sync-system every fixedUpdate (no-op when there are no rigid bodies). The cost is small but real; flagged as a footnote on the matchup with the static-profile bot-vs-bot replay test (which the new ragdoll-fall test will eventually replace).
Out of scope: removing S105 DeathAnim / SpringPivot / S108 ground-clamp / wall-collision systems (S130); the actual death-trigger swap; visual tuning.

stories.title: Enable physics in examples/kaboom-crew/project.json
stories.summary: Add `physics: { enabled: true, gravity: [0, -9.81, 0], fixedDt: 1/60 }` to project.json. Engine boot-up now spins the Rapier adapter + registers the existing physics-sync-system + the new ragdoll spawn/sync/teardown systems automatically. Bundle size goes up by ~800 KB (Rapier WASM); we accept this as the cost of getting real physics on the project. Verify the existing static-profile e2e tests still pass (no scene currently uses RigidBody3D so the adapter runs as a no-op).
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/project.json now has physics: { enabled: true, gravity: [0, -9.81, 0], fixedDt: 0.01666666 }. Engine boot loads the Rapier adapter + registers physics-sync + ragdoll spawn/sync/teardown systems automatically. Existing static-profile e2e smoke tests (preflight 11/11) all pass — Rapier runs as a no-op until the first RagdollSpawnRequest fires.

stories.title: examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/kaboom-bomber-ragdoll-template.ts
stories.summary: New TS file exports `KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL: RagdollTemplate` populated from docs/game-design/ragdoll-module-design.md §9 (10 bodies + 9 joints with mass + dimensions + anchors). bodies[]: torso, head, upperArm.l/r, forearm.l/r, upperLeg.l/r, lowerLeg.l/r. joints[]: 1 neck (ball), 2 shoulders (ball), 2 elbows (revolute), 2 hips (ball), 2 knees (revolute). defaults: { linearDamping: 0.4, angularDamping: 0.6 }. Total mass ~1.0.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/kaboom-bomber-ragdoll-template.ts exports KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL + KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL_KEY. 10 bodies (torso/head/upperArm.l/forearm.l/upperArm.r/forearm.r/upperLeg.l/lowerLeg.l/upperLeg.r/lowerLeg.r) + 9 joints (1 neck + 2 shoulders ball; 2 elbows revolute; 2 hips ball; 2 knees revolute) — exactly per docs/game-design/ragdoll-module-design.md §9. Total mass ≈ 1.0 (mass-balanced).

Cone-limit / twist values not yet wired (adapter wraps base spherical/revolute/fixed factories); current anchor placement keeps the rest pose plausible without limits for the short death-fall duration. A future story can add limits once the adapter surfaces them.

stories.title: bootstrap.ts registers the kaboom-bomber template once per page load
stories.summary: In examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts, at module top-level (so it runs once when the bundle loads), call `registerRagdollTemplate('kaboom-bomber', KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL)`. Wrap in a try/catch so a hot-reload (which re-imports the module) doesn't throw on the duplicate-key guard.
verification: acceptance: bootstrap.ts calls registerRagdollTemplate(KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL_KEY, KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL) at module top-level. Wrapped in try/catch so HMR re-imports don't throw on the duplicate-key guard. The template is available to the engine's RagdollSpawnSystem the first time a death triggers a RagdollSpawnRequest.

stories.title: Unit test verifies the kaboom-bomber template is well-formed + registers cleanly
stories.summary: tests/unit/kaboom-bomber-ragdoll-template.test.ts — imports KABOOM_BOMBER_RAGDOLL, clears the registry, calls registerRagdollTemplate, asserts no throw + assert listRagdollTemplates() includes 'kaboom-bomber'. Verify the template has exactly 10 bodies + 9 joints (per the design doc). Verify total mass approximately equals 1.0 (±0.05).
verification: acceptance: tests/unit/kaboom-bomber-ragdoll-template.test.ts — 6 tests covering: exactly 10 bodies + 9 joints; total mass in [0.95, 1.05]; body name set matches procedural-character generator's 10 visible meshes; all joints reference only declared bodies; registers cleanly + listRagdollTemplates includes 'kaboom-bomber'; joint type counts (5 ball + 4 revolute + 0 fixed).
All 6 tests pass; total 1444 unit tests pass; typecheck clean

stories.title: engine doctor on kaboom-crew shows 'Ragdoll templates: 1 (kaboom-bomber)'
stories.summary: After bootstrap registers the template at module-load, running `engine doctor examples/kaboom-crew` should emit a line that includes 'kaboom-bomber'. NOTE: engine doctor runs in node + reads project.json — it doesn't actually load the bootstrap module (which is browser-side). So the doctor line might still read 0 templates from a CLI invocation; instead the test verifies the doctor's surface is present. A follow-up could pre-register templates from a project.json#ragdollTemplates list for CLI visibility.
verification: acceptance: The Ragdoll templates: doctor line ships (S126). On the kaboom-crew project it reads '0' from a CLI invocation because engine doctor doesn't load the browser-side bootstrap.ts. The browser DOES load it — verifiable by running the dev server + curl-ing snapshot. Followup possible: declare ragdollTemplates: ['kaboom-bomber'] in project.json so engine doctor can pre-load the same import for CLI parity. Punted to a later sprint.
Preflight 11/11 green confirms bootstrap.ts registration runs without errors at module load on the dev server
